name: Correspondent and Nested Banking
description: Abuse of correspondent banking relationships, including nested or downstream use of a respondent's account by other institutions, to move illicit funds across borders with limited visibility of the underlying customers and purposes. Payable-through accounts and shell bank links add risk.

sources.text: FATF, Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services (2016)
Wolfsberg Group, Correspondent Banking Due Diligence Questionnaire (CBDDQ) (current version, specify year)
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Guidelines: Sound management of risks related to money laundering and financing of terrorism (2014, rev. 2020)

exposure.rationale: Respondent and nested bank/PSP flows via correspondent accounts over SWIFT.

indicators.name: Respondent serves undisclosed downstream institutions
indicators.desc: Respondent provides access to its account for other banks or payment firms (nesting) without disclosure.
indicators.ctx: Respondent provides access to its account for other banks or payment firms (nesting) without disclosure.
indicators.fp: Group and agency arrangements are disclosed normally.

indicators.name: Respondent based in high-risk jurisdiction with weak AML supervision
indicators.canon: Counterparty or flows in higher-risk jurisdictions with weak AML controls
indicators.desc: Funds, counterparties or institutions are located in jurisdictions with weak AML supervision, sanctions exposure or limited VASP regulation.
indicators.ctx: Respondent operates where regulation or supervision is weak.
indicators.fp: Large regional banks in higher-risk countries serve real trade.

indicators.name: Transaction volumes disproportionate to respondent's size
indicators.canon: Transaction volumes disproportionate to respondent's size
indicators.desc: Flows far exceed expected levels for the respondent's balance sheet or footprint.
indicators.ctx: Flows far exceed expected levels for the respondent's balance sheet or footprint.

indicators.name: Missing or poor-quality payment message information
indicators.canon: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information
indicators.desc: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.
indicators.ctx: Messages lack originator or beneficiary data or use unclear references.

indicators.name: Pooled flows with frequent round-sum payments
indicators.canon: Pooled flows with frequent round-sum payments
indicators.desc: Large round-value payments or repeated amounts for multiple unrelated beneficiaries.
indicators.ctx: Large round-value payments or repeated amounts for multiple unrelated beneficiaries.

indicators.name: Respondent refuses or delays information requests
indicators.canon: Refusal or delay in answering due diligence requests
indicators.desc: Customer or counterparty delays, refuses or gives incomplete or evasive responses to KYC, refresh or request-for-information enquiries.
indicators.ctx: Slow, evasive or incomplete responses to RFIs.

indicators.name: Links to shell banks or unlicensed entities
indicators.canon: Links to shell banks or unlicensed entities
indicators.desc: Respondent has relationships with shell or unlicensed institutions.
indicators.ctx: Respondent has relationships with shell or unlicensed institutions.

indicators.name: Payable-through account use by respondent's customers
indicators.canon: Payable-through or pooled access enabling third-party payments
indicators.desc: Underlying customers of another party transact directly through payable-through, pooled or payment-agent facilities.
indicators.ctx: Respondent's customers transact directly through the account.

indicators.name: Adverse media or enforcement on respondent
indicators.canon: Adverse media or intelligence linking counterparties to criminal activity
indicators.desc: Counterparties, suppliers, respondents or controllers appear in adverse media, law-enforcement notices or intelligence connected to financial crime, abuse, forced labour or organised crime.
indicators.ctx: Respondent has regulatory action, sanctions or ML scandals.
